workout.warmup: First 5 min of the cardio piece, easy. That is the warmup.
workout.coach_note: You trained lower Sunday and upper yesterday, so today is cardio - same reasoning as two weeks ago. 48 hours is thin for another heavy squat day and your Wednesday session deserves fresh legs, because it is a big one. Now the actual news from your backlog, and it is good. YOUR SCAPULA IS CLEARED. Across four sessions you did chest-supported rows, front pulldowns, cable rows at 145, lat pulldowns, PULL-UPS, hanging knee raises, skull crushers, and you hoisted 60 lb dumbbells into a press - and reported zero pain on any of it. Skull crushers and heavy DB hoisting were both on the restricted list. They are off it. Second: your bench moved. 185 for 9 and 9 yesterday against 185 for 5/5/5/4 on Aug 2 - that is not a good day, that is a different lift. Same story on the shoulder press, where 60 lb dumbbells gave you 10 reps and 60 flatly failed you back on Jul 22. Third: your squat at 205 gave you 8/8/10 on Sunday with your BEST set last, which means you left reps there. One thing has not moved: the leg curl. You earned 80 lb on Aug 16 with a clean 12/12/12 and you have run 70 in every session since - 12/10/10, then 12/11. Travel machines are part of it, but it is now the only lift in your program that has gone nowhere in a month. Wednesday it goes to 80 and I do not want to see 70 again.

exercises.name: Steady-State Cardio - ZONE 2
exercises.detail: 35-40 min. Elliptical, bike, or incline treadmill.
exercises.note: Conversational the whole way - full sentences without gasping. No intervals, no sprints, no stair-climber grinding. Wednesday is a heavy squat day and your legs need to arrive fresh. Rower is fine again now that the scapula is clear, if you want the variety - but keep it steady-state, not a hard pull.

exercises.name: Thoracic Mobility
exercises.detail: Thread-the-Needle x 8/side, Open Book rotation x 8/side, foam roll upper back x 8 passes
exercises.note: Thread-the-needle is the kneeling one you did on your own in Boston - arm behind the head, rotate up and across. Good instinct, keep it. Your scapular tissue has failed twice this summer and thoracic mobility is the cheapest insurance against a third. Ten minutes, twice a week, indefinitely.

exercises.name: Core Circuit
exercises.detail: 2 rounds: Pallof Press 22.5 lb x 12/side, Kettlebell Plank Drag x 20 (30 lb), Dead Bugs x 24
exercises.note: The Boston circuit - you bumped the KB drag to 30 lb because 20 felt light, so 30 is the number now. Hips stay square on the drag, do not let them rotate as you reach under. Optional if you are short on time.
